speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash, such as whether it is red, raised, or blistered? Also, have you started any new medications or foods in the last few weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash have a "slapped cheek" appearance on the face, and does the body rash look like a lacy or net-like pattern? Also, has she been exposed to anyone with similar symptoms recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a lacy, pruritic body rash is classic for Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
